I’m not sure this film should be classified as horror; to me it was more of a disturbing drama sprinkled with a handful of gory murders. Just as with “X”, the previous film that kicked off the trilogy of which “Pearl” is the second entry, a great deal of the film was spent building plot and the first murder occurred exactly at the one-hour mark. I don’t think anyone can deny that this film looks REALLY good. Other reviewers who note a resemblance to “The Wizard of Oz” are not to be commended on their keen perception; the director made it absolutely clear that is what he was going for. From the opening shot which mirrors Dorothy‘s arrival in Oz to the vintage title fonts and styles to the sumptuous colors throughout, one half expects a group of Munchkins to emerge from the cornfield at any time. While I felt that Jenna Ortega might have possessed greater screen presence in the first movie despite her smaller part, there is no rival to Mia Goth in this one. She owns the screen and creates a complex and (almost) sympathetic character in Pearl. It would be interesting to rewatch “X” with an eye on the older version of the character, which I did not even realize on the first viewing was played by Mia Goth. That shows you how keen my perception is. The conventional wisdom of all reviews I have seen is that “Maxxxine”, the third film in the trilogy, is the weakest of the three. But as “X” was good enough to get me to watch “Pearl”, so “Pearl” is good enough to carry me through to finish the trilogy.

I wanted to feel it, not just hear it all explained in that long one-take monologue (still an amazing performance, though). It’s eerie. Her stance, her stares, that’s everything this film is. That’s what creates all the horror. But the whys and hows still left me with way too many questions.
